subject.title: Feature: Subscribe to WhatsApp call events (Baileys)

question: Should inbound WhatsApp Baileys call events be exposed to agents, and which opt-in, retention, filtering, and hook/tool/session surface should own sanitized call activity?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but call metadata is privacy-sensitive and the permanent exposure surface is a product/security boundary that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Plugin-owned opt-in call activity
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default WhatsApp plugin path that subscribes to Baileys `call`, sanitizes events, enforces existing access controls, and exposes only the approved activity surface.

options.title: Defer inbound call tracking
options.body: Keep outbound MeowCaller support only and leave this issue open or close it only after maintainers decide contact-history call tracking is out of scope.

options.title: External plugin or API proposal first
options.body: Require a separate plugin/API design if maintainers want inbound call tracking outside the bundled WhatsApp plugin.

recommendation.title: Plugin-owned opt-in call activity
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default WhatsApp plugin path that subscribes to Baileys `call`, sanitizes events, enforces existing access controls, and exposes only the approved activity surface.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history and issue discussion tie this person to WhatsApp call surfaces and the maintainer-facing product/security decision.
